groups.title: Eye drops (D54000COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for tired eyes, redness of the conjunctiva, discomfort of the eye after swimming or when dust or sweat has got into the eye, inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet and other light, soreness of the eyelids, discomfort when hard contact lenses are worn, itching of the eye, and blurring of the eye (for example when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops into the eye at a time, 5 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe pain in the eye, if you have had allergic symptoms to an eye medicine (for example redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, reddening), if you have glaucoma, or if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had it. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses, and do not use it while soft contact lenses are being worn. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible. Do not use it after the expiry date, and once it has been opened use it as soon as possible.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Tired eyes, conjunctival redness, eye inflammation from light, sore eyelids, itching and blurring, and eye discomfort after swimming or from dust

groups.title: Tablet (E88900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat (pain in the throat), cough, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Those over 7 years of age and under 15 years of age: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, you must consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
If a serious skin reaction that can very rarely be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis — occurs, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have ever had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or kidney failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If symptoms do not improve after 5 or 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, shock (hives, swelling, tightness of the chest, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, sweating and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction (generalised weakness, jaundice) or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, oedema, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are an older person; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; if you have symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like); if you have had insomnia, dizziness, weakness, tremor or palpitations with cold medicines, cough and expectorant medicines or oral medicines for rhinitis; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine) or have had an allergic reaction to it; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life; for poor growth of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; for beriberi and tired eyes; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Those aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have kidney stones or severe kidney failure; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have hypersensitivity to soya-bean oil or have had an allergic reaction to it; or if you have hypersensitivity to soya or peanut.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, a low protein level in the blood, diabetes, gout, or kidney stones now or in the past; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or fat emulsions have to be given to you.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen.
Taking it together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene may cause a high potassium level in the blood, so consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening, loose stools, stomatitis, loss of appetite, a feeling of abdominal bloating, low blood pressure, flushing of the face, an irregular heartbeat, a skin rash, red patches, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced function of the central nervous system, dermatitis, an unpleasant smell of sweat or breath, hair loss, impatience, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
